Buckle up because here's a story; some pre-face, this takes place in the past and I was, at the time, quite young. Ever since I started the game I've had questing, and subsequently lore, as my primary reason to play the game; this being the case, my stats and thus money making methods until I achieved my goal of all quests completed were very lacking. Come the latter half of that era it was announced that a new skill was coming to the game, a skill I was very excited for based on core concepts and of course a skill cape with an animal icon was a good goal for me at the time. As I mentioned, my money making methods were severely under-par as I did not boss or skill efficiently and my primary source was clue rewards; that is, until I discovered a new money making method in the wake of trade limits and the task sets. My new method of making money involved my close knit group of friends and myself hacking away at the brush looking for a specific resource, an item needed for the task sets yet uncommonly brought into the game. Each resource was worth, at the time, a significant amount of coins and with proper timing one plant could be harvested by every person present! We made a good chunk of change in the month we did this method, and subsequently I gathered literally thousands of a byproduct item as a byproduct of our hacking away. By the end of that year I had amassed well over 35k of these useless items with the assumption they were just a pointless byproduct of our gathering; I eventually dropped them sometime before the new skill came out. Going by the prices of just today that amount is a large sum, back then they worth well over a massive amount not to mention the GP value was higher back then. TL;DR: Amassed 35k "useless" items, dropped them on a whim assuming they'd always be useless, lost out on a massive amount gp in that year.
I sure as sugar wouldn't have taken until a later year to max most skills lol. Ah well, it's funny looking back but had my younger self fully appreciated that loss I'd have been mad.

Out of all these this is the one I'm going to have to disagree with the most. The type of scheduling that gives us a few episodes then goes on months of hiatus is not a good model. Shows that don't actively need to adapt to week to week changes, let's use a fast-paced animated comedy as an example, can get by with not making entire seasons in advanced for reasons essentially stemming from animation quality cuts and story flexibility (having vaguely constrained "arcs" and more or less social commentary otherwise.) With shows focused more on emotion depth, story arcs, and character development, let's use a dramatic animated series as the example here, entire seasons need to be made and put out in a set order with little room for significant rewrites or edits once the product is made and put out for view. But that's just my two cents; if I had my way shows would release entire seasons for view at once so I can binge the information at once, though I can see where that has its own can of worms for writing.

Microtransactions are not going away, and only SHOULD be toned down in frequency or at the least be given a precise schedule for the repeated exp heavy ones. Hitting the level cap on skills to access content at those levels is what most strive for and the more people at higher levels the better as it justifies more content for higher levels.  TL;DR - It all depends on personal choice and personal arbitrary assigned values to inherently valueless pixels. It's a game, play it to unlock stuff to have fun or to do personal goals.
